narrativeReportMd:
# Duration R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local hard instance-breaking change was found for `Duration`. The datatype remains the same non-abstract specialization of `Quantity`, with the same root cardinality, same local `drt-1` invariant, and the same primary `duration-units` binding strength and code list.

## Scope
The assessment covers the `Duration` StructureDefinition root differential and Duration-owned unit bindings. Changes inherited from `Quantity`, `Element`, and `Extension` are excluded from `findings[]` and delegated to their own artifact reports.

## Main migration themes
FHIR instance data using `Duration` should not need a local Duration-specific transform. The main local migration concern is for conformance tooling that reads StructureDefinitions: the R4 maximum value set extension is represented in R6 as `ElementDefinition.binding.additional` with purpose `maximum`.

## Highest-impact findings
There are no Critical or High local findings. The single local finding is a Low-impact metadata/codegen compatibility issue, not an instance validation break.

## Findings requiring human review
No local finding requires human review. Confidence is limited mainly by the absence of a live UCUM expansion for the filtered maximum value set and absence of an official rendered diff.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 binding representation change appears to be a justified move to the native additional-binding model. Keeping the legacy extension as a duplicate could have helped older tooling but would also preserve obsolete metadata conventions.

## Follow-up analysis
The `Quantity` report should own inherited child-element changes, especially the added comparator code `ad` and the new `qty-4` warning.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No local R4-valid `Duration` instance pattern was found that becomes invalid in R6 because of a Duration-owned change. The only local finding is a Low-impact StructureDefinition metadata change: the maximum binding moved from an R4 extension to R6 `binding.additional`. The main uncertainty is terminology expansion behavior for UCUM filtered value sets.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Instance migration is expected to be no-op for local Duration rules: keep `value`, `system`, and UCUM time `code` content as before. Conformance tooling should update binding readers to understand R6 additional bindings and should not rely solely on the R4 `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension. Separately, systems must evaluate inherited `Quantity` changes in the `Quantity` report.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is High for StructureDefinition-level conclusions because both assigned StructureDefinitions and their package-index entries were present and directly compared. Confidence is Medium for terminology expansion edge cases because `all-time-units` is a UCUM filter (`canonical = a`) and no live expansion was performed.

findings.title: Duration maximum unit binding moved from R4 extension to R6 additional binding metadata

oldState.summary: The root Duration binding was extensible to duration-units and expressed the maximum all-time-units binding using the R4 elementdefinition-maxValueSet extension.
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, the local `Duration` root binding points to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/duration-units` and carries `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/elementdefinition-maxValueSet` with value `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-time-units`.

newState.summary: The root Duration binding remains extensible to duration-units, and the same maximum all-time-units binding is represented as ElementDefinition.binding.additional with purpose maximum.
newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the same maximum value set appears in `binding.additional[0]` with `purpose` = `maximum` and `valueSet` = `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-time-units`. The primary binding canonical and strength did not change.

facts.note: Metadata representation changed from an R4 extension to native R6 additional binding.
The explicit UCUM code list was unchanged.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new elements are the same root element `Duration`; both use the same primary and maximum binding canonicals. Only the ElementDefinition metadata location for the maximum binding changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a FHIR instance validation break: an instance using a Duration code from the unchanged local binding is affected the same way. The risk is for validators, documentation generators, profile comparison tools, or code generators that consume StructureDefinitions and only know the R4 `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension; those tools may miss the maximum binding in R6 until updated to read `binding.additional`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: No direct clinical or business data loss was identified because the allowed Duration instance content did not change locally.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent additional terminology bindings using the native R6 ElementDefinition additional-binding model rather than the older extension.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4 Duration instance-shape alternative is needed because the primary and maximum unit bindings preserve the same instance content.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal--representing maximum and other additional terminology bindings in the native `ElementDefinition.binding.additional` model--is reasonable, and the level of breakage is low. The primary `duration-units` binding and maximum `all-time-units` canonical are preserved, so this does not make R4-valid `Duration` instance data invalid in R6. The compatibility burden is on StructureDefinition consumers that must update their metadata readers, which is probably justified for a first-class R6 binding representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: There is not a distinct less-breaking base R6 design needed for `Duration` instance compatibility: the allowed Duration instance content did not change. The apparent alternative of also publishing the legacy R4 `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension in R6 would mainly support older conformance tooling; it would not preserve otherwise-invalid R4 instances. Dual-publishing the extension and `binding.additional[purpose=maximum]` would also create duplicate same-resource metadata, with risk of disagreement and prolonged dependence on the legacy extension, so it is better treated as migration mitigation rather than a backwards-compatible base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping the old maxValueSet extension as duplicate R6 metadata could help legacy conformance tooling, but that is a transition mitigation with duplication and inconsistency risk.

evidence.detail: R4 root binding is extensible to duration-units and uses elementdefinition-maxValueSet for all-time-units.
R6 root binding is extensible to the same duration-units ValueSet and carries additional[purpose=maximum] for all-time-units.
The explicit Duration unit code list is unchanged: ms, s, min, h, d, wk, mo, a.
The maximum binding ValueSet continues to use the same UCUM filter: canonical = a.

examples.examplesMd: No instance fragment is shown because the change affects StructureDefinition metadata consumers, not the JSON/XML shape of `Duration` values.

findings.narrativeMd: `Duration` still points to the same primary and maximum unit value sets, but the R6 StructureDefinition stores the maximum binding in a different place. This can surprise tooling that extracts Duration unit constraints from raw ElementDefinition JSON because a simple R4-era scan for `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` will no longer find the maximum binding.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `Duration` instance does not become invalid in R6 because of this local change. Conversely, the local Duration binding change does not create new R6 instance content that cannot be represented in R4. The compatibility issue is limited to conformance-resource processing: tools must read R6 `binding.additional` to preserve the same validation intent.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update StructureDefinition parsers and validation metadata extraction to map R4 `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` and R6 `binding.additional[purpose=maximum]` to the same internal concept. Regression tests should verify that the primary extensible binding and maximum all-time-units binding are both detected for `Duration` in R6.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was probably part of a general R6 move to first-class additional bindings. A backward-compatible transition could have retained the legacy extension in R6, but that would duplicate binding metadata and risk conflicts. Since the instance semantics are unchanged, updating tooling is the cleaner long-term approach.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The R4 and R6 `Duration` root binding continue to use the same extensible `duration-units` ValueSet and the same maximum `all-time-units` ValueSet. The change is that R4 expressed the maximum binding through the legacy `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension, while R6 expresses it through `ElementDefinition.binding.additional[purpose=maximum]`. A StructureDefinition reader that only scans the R4 extension could miss the maximum binding until updated, but R4-valid Duration instance data is not made invalid and the semantic constraint is preserved.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition-Duration.json snapshot `Duration.binding` has the same primary ValueSet and `binding.additional[0].purpose=maximum` with `valueSet=http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-time-units`.
R4 and R6 ValueSet-duration-units.json list the same UCUM concepts: ms, s, min, h, d, wk, mo, a.
R4 and R6 ValueSet-all-time-units.json both use the same UCUM canonical filter `canonical = a`.
Local R4 maturity metadata marks Duration as normative with normativeVersion 4.0.0.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Duration is normative in R4, so direct instance or semantic breaks would need strong justification. Here the normative stability concern is softened because the instance-level binding target and maximum binding meaning are unchanged; the burden is limited to metadata consumers learning the R6-native additional-binding representation.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling: conformance tooling that reads raw ElementDefinition JSON and only recognizes the R4 maxValueSet extension may miss the maximum binding in R6, but validators using the R6 StructureDefinition model can read the equivalent `binding.additional` metadata and no old-valid/new-invalid Duration instance break is apparent.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Dual-publishing the old maxValueSet extension alongside the R6 `binding.additional` entry could reduce friction for legacy metadata readers, but it would duplicate the same constraint in two places, create consistency risk, and prolong dependence on an R4-era extension. Because instance compatibility is already preserved and the R6-native representation is the relevant base-model goal, no less-breaking base R6 design is needed.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing low-impact/runtime-tooling assessment and with the conclusion that no instance-preserving alternative is needed; the fresh judgment frames this as metadata/tooling churn rather than a meaningful compatibility problem.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, immediate base definition (`Quantity`), derivation, and non-abstract flag are unchanged. The R6 StructureDefinition is present at the expected path and in the package index.

Both snapshots contain the same Duration element ids: root, `id`, `extension`, `value`, `comparator`, `unit`, `system`, and `code`. The local differential in both versions contains only the root `Duration` element.
The root remains `0..*`. No local Duration-owned child cardinality change was found; child cardinalities are inherited from `Quantity` or `Element`.
`Duration` remains a specialization of `Quantity`. No local choice type, primitive type, or reference target domain change applies to this datatype.

The root binding strength remains `extensible` and the primary value set remains `duration-units`. The explicit `duration-units` UCUM codes are unchanged. The maximum value set remains `all-time-units` with the same UCUM filter, but no live expansion was performed for the filter.

The Duration-owned invariant `drt-1` has the same severity, human text, and FHIRPath expression. R6 adds a `source` field and omits the R4 XPath representation; that is metadata/formula-presentation change, not a local validation change.
No fixed value, pattern, or default value was found on the local Duration root in either version.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex restriction was added, removed, or changed for `Duration`.
The root `Duration` element remains `isModifier=false`. The inherited `Duration.comparator` modifier status is owned by `Quantity` and is out of scope for local findings.
No local root summary-flag change was found. Inherited child summary flags remain a Quantity/Element concern.
No local Duration slicing was introduced or removed.

The local root short text and definition remain `A length of time`. The package-level description was shortened from `Base StructureDefinition for Duration Type: A length of time.` to `Duration Type: A length of time.`, which does not alter instance conformance.
No local Duration instance serialization change was found. The only local serialization/codegen issue is the StructureDefinition metadata move for the maximum binding, reported separately.

No local Duration-owned element, type, or code addition creates a new R6 Duration instance shape that R4 cannot represent. Inherited Quantity changes, especially comparator `ad`, are out of scope and should be assessed under `Quantity`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds type-characteristics metadata for Duration
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds metadata extensions indicating characteristics such as `has-range`, `is-continuous`, and `has-units`. These describe the datatype for tooling and documentation but do not add required instance content or change validation of existing Duration values.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators and model documentation tools may be able to use these flags, but they should not treat them as new JSON/XML elements.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Duration unit ValueSet description is clarified while the code list stays the same
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 description broadly said the value set included all UCUM codes, while R6 clarifies that it is the common UCUM codes used for Duration. The computable compose list is unchanged, so validators using the ValueSet content should behave the same.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation or UI text generated from ValueSet descriptions may change wording, but no code migration is indicated for `ms`, `s`, `min`, `h`, `d`, `wk`, `mo`, or `a`.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `Duration` inherits `value`, `comparator`, `unit`, `system`, and `code` from `Quantity`. R6 Quantity-related changes visible in the Duration snapshot, including comparator code `ad`, the `qty-4` warning, and Quantity's own base-definition shift, should be assessed in the `Quantity` report rather than duplicated here.

The maximum binding `all-time-units` is defined by a UCUM filter (`canonical = a`). A live terminology-server expansion would confirm whether the practical expanded set changed between the terminology versions used with R4 and R6.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official rendered R4-to-R6 diff page or ballot change note was used, so the analysis is based on package artifacts rather than committee-authored migration notes.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official Duration datatype diff or R6 ballot change log if available.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The filtered `all-time-units` ValueSet was compared by its compose filter, not by live expansion. If the UCUM terminology server's interpretation of `canonical = a` changed, practical validation behavior could differ even though the FHIR ValueSet filter text is unchanged.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Expand `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-time-units` for both version contexts against the intended UCUM terminology source and compare the expanded codes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is `6.0.0-ballot4`, not a final normative release. Ballot content may still change before publication.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Repeat the comparison against the final R6 core package when published.
